verdict.rationale: Lium has its own background lifecycle automations: pods auto-delete on a TTL, end time, or USD spend cap, and volumes are backed up every 6 hours. Its SDK and agent flow can rent a node, run a job, and tear the pod down without a browser, within server-enforced budgets. But the multi-step automation is driven by the user's external agent or script calling these primitives, not by a first-party automation feature. missing for 10: scheduled or recurring job triggers, an event-driven or background workflow engine, monitoring or notification of autonomous runs, independent or hands-on corroboration.
